title: The rosary, again
hookLine: the beads have become a road
tomorrow: which psalm do you send a scared friend at midnight?

cards: The night before something big, sleep won't come. The scroll, the ceiling, the replay of every mistake. Some people reach for a playlist.

Sofia's abuela reaches for a string of beads worn smooth. Can a string of beads turn into a road? The rosary has come back again and again on this path, and by now the beads can be more than a way of counting.

teach.b: The road runs through Jesus's life. Each stretch of beads holds a scene, called a mystery: the joyful ones, his birth and childhood; the sorrowful ones, his suffering; the glorious ones, Easter and after.
One to tell a friend: Pope John Paul the Second added another set, the luminous mysteries, the mysteries of light, from Jesus's baptism and the wedding at Cana to the Last Supper.
He wrote that the rosary is a way of looking at the face of Christ with Mary, and echoed an earlier pope who called it a summary of the whole Gospel. The model is Mary herself.
Luke says, in the Douay-Rheims: "But Mary kept all these words, pondering them in her heart." That's what the beads are for.

The Hail Marys keep the lips and fingers busy, so the mind can walk the scene: the stable, the garden, the empty tomb. Here's where it meets a hard week. A worry doesn't vanish when the beads come out.
But it gets company. An anxious night can walk beside his night in the garden of Gethsemane; a new start, beside the empty tomb.
Bead by bead, a scattered mind gets a road.

how: Catholics pray the rosary alone, as families or in parish groups, often one set of mysteries a day; a full rosary walks through one set, with an Our Father, Hail Marys and a Glory Be for each mystery.

o: beads walking through Jesus's life with Mary
a counting game to finish prayers quickly
a necklace Catholics wear for protection

games.q: the road of beads — tap the pairs.

s: the rosary's scenes are mostly about Mary's own life
the road runs through Jesus's life: birth, light, suffering, Easter. Mary walks it with you.
Pope John Paul II added the luminous mysteries, the mysteries of light

games.q: your cousin says the rosary is 'just the same prayer over and over. what's the point?' best answer?
o: the repeats keep lips and fingers busy, so the mind can walk a scene of Jesus's life.
each repeat earns a little more grace, so more is always better.
it's mainly a prayer to Mary instead of a prayer about Jesus.
games.why: Mary kept all these words, pondering them in her heart. the beads hold the hands still so the heart can ponder.

practice: Hold a rosary if you have one, or let your fingers walk along your knuckles. Pick one mystery that fits this week, a joyful one or a sorrowful one, and let each bead or knuckle be one step through that scene.
If you pray, say a Hail Mary at each; if not, walk the scene slowly in your mind.

wordCard.voice: The rosary. A road of beads through the life of Jesus, walked beside Mary one scene at a time.

orig.note: Greek: she kept, held close. Luke's word for what Mary did with all these words.

carryVoice: Hold onto this: the road of beads, where a worry walks beside his story. See you tomorrow.

sources.q: But Mary kept all these words, pondering them in her heart.
